data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Chemical agents, peels & baths_

**Class:** Combination superficial peeling agent: resorcinol 14% + salicylic acid 14% + lactic acid 14% in ethanol

## Mechanism of action
- Keratolytic action of all three components → superficial exfoliation; resorcinol also weakens hydrogen bonds of keratin

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Superficial peel for acne, comedones, PIH, melasma, mild photoageing
- As a primer before 35% TCA (Monheit medium-depth peel)

## Dose & formulations
- 1–3 coats, depending on response (erythema → patchy frosting); no neutralisation needed

## Adverse effects
- Burning, erythema, peeling; salicylism (large areas); resorcinol — contact allergy, thyroid effects, ochronosis (rare)

## Contraindications
- Resorcinol/salicylate allergy, pregnancy (salicylate), active infection

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid (salicylate).

## Viva points
- Composition: resorcinol + salicylic + lactic acid 14% each
- Jessner + TCA 35% = Monheit peel

_Sources: Khopkar ch.31 (Combination peeling agents); Wolverton 4e ch.53. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
